narrative:
The model determined that you have a 68% chance of representing a bad credit risk. Because this probability is well above the approval threshold, your loan application was denied.

The three factors that most strongly influenced this outcome were your credit history, the status of your checking account, and the purpose of the loan. Your credit history showed that all previous credits at this bank have been paid, which is relatively uncommon. Unfortunately, in this dataset that specific history pushed the prediction toward higher risk. The status of your checking account, sitting between 0 and 200 DM, also increased the likelihood of being classified as bad credit compared with applicants who maintain no checking account or hold larger balances. Finally, the fact that you are requesting the loan to purchase a new car further contributed to the negative decision; new-car loans are associated with higher risk in the patterns the model has learned.

Taken together, these three pieces of information outweighed several positive signals such as your modest loan amount, steady employment, and limited financial dependents.

To improve your chances on a future application, focus first on building a longer track record of on-time payments that matches the “existing paid” profile most commonly seen among approved applicants. Maintaining a healthier checking-account balance and considering a different loan purpose may also help. Once these areas show clearer improvement, you are welcome to reapply.
